deviations: Table 1 (pisa_full_gps_final.dta, 2.47 GB) cannot be read in full through the read-only mount within the 300 s sandbox limit (raw I/O roughly 5-15 MB/s; fread select= on the 2.8 GB CSV and haven col_select on the .dta both timed out). The final script parses the Stata 118 file directly, reading only the 14 needed columns from evenly spread blocks of 3000 consecutive rows (van der Corput order) until a 225 s deadline: 1,965,000 of 1,992,276 rows (98.6%), all 49 countries. Table 1 coefficients are therefore estimated on that subsample.
table1_col3_observations is the .dta header row count (1,992,276), reported because no row read has a missing regression variable; it is not the N of the subsample regression (1,965,000).

Table 1 standard errors are clustered on the country-level (patience, risk-taking) pair (49 distinct values) instead of the country string, which is a Stata strL that the direct parser does not decode. Coefficients are unaffected.

Table 2 uses the full migrant file (pisa_full_gps_final_imcoo.dta read with haven col_select) with no deviation: reg pv1math prefs female age imfemale image coo_oecd i.countrywave, cluster(coo) as feols(... | countrywave, cluster=~coo, fixef.rm='none'); image is constant (0) in this sample and drops for collinearity, as in Stata.
notes: Seeded mode, following 3_analysis_crosscountry.do (Table 1: reg pv1math prefs female age migra1 migra2 image imfemale immigra1 i.wave [pw=wgtc], cluster(country); natives: migra0==1 without migration controls) and 3_analysis_migrants.do (Table 2). Attempts 1-3 were exploratory (no RESULT lines): 1 and 2 timed out reading the big file; 3 measured raw I/O and the .dta header. Attempt 4 (claim): 43% row subsample, and the strL bug gave a wrong cluster id; fixed cluster id and raised the read deadline. One run with deadline 262 s (02:07) hung during a Docker Desktop daemon wedge (container still up hours later) and a second launch never started a container; per the coordinator these are not attempts and are excluded (scratch copy kept outside the run dir). After the restart the deadline was set to 225 s. Attempt 5 (claim): 79.5% subsample in 12000-row blocks covered only 48 countries, so risk-taking was off; changed to 3000-row blocks. Final: 98.6% of rows, 49 countries; Table 2 reproduces exactly, Table 1 within about 0.01 of the claims except col1 patience 0.921 vs 0.917 and col2 risk -0.477 vs -0.482.
